entities.name: Hermanafrid
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Hermanfrid (Hermanafrid) was the last independent king of the Thuringii in early sixth-century central Germany, one of three sons of King Bisinus. Through marriage to Amalaberga, niece of the Ostrogothic king Theodoric the Great, he entered the web of post-Roman dynastic alliances that linked Thuringians, Ostrogoths, and Merovingian Franks.

Rivalry with his brothers and Frankish expansion under Theuderic I ended Thuringian autonomy: Frankish armies crushed Thuringian power (c. 531), and Hermanfrid was killed after defeat—tradition places his death near Zülpich. The kingdom was partitioned into Frankish domination, erasing Thuringia as an independent gentile monarchy.

Hermanfrid thus marks the terminus of Thuringian kingship and the Merovingian absorption of a major Elbe–Saale people into the Frankish sphere—a key step in the making of early medieval Germany.
